newsitem.title: THAILAND: Rights groups call for more pressure on Burma.
newsitem.headline: Rights groups call for more pressure on Burma.

text.p: Various human rights groups marked Burma's 49th anniversary of independence on Saturday by calling on international community to put more pressure on the nation's military regime.
Among the pleas they made included an end to the Association of South East Asian Nations' (ASEAN) so-called constructive engagement policy and economic sanction.

"If both sticks and carrots will be used with Burma, I would like to request that carrots be given piece by piece. We should not give them the whole jackpot," said Debbie Stothard, a co-ordinator of Alternative ASEAN Network on Burma.
The group, which campaigns to end human rights abuses in Burma, comprises 46 organizations in 20 countries.
Burma's military-led State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) seized power after crushing pro-democracy uprisings in September 1988.
Although the military junta held election in 1990 in which Aung San Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy (NLD) won a landslide victory, it refused to recognize the result of the poll.
About 50 Burmese students also held a rally on Saturday in front of the Burmese Embassy in Bangkok calling for democracy.

"We demand that the military dictator hand over the state power to the people's elected party members and unconditionally release all imprisoned students and political activists," a student leader said.
The students also urged the international community to suspend investments in Burma until power is transferred to a democratically-elected government.
At the same time the U.S.-based Human Rights Watch called on the Thai government to improve protection for Burmese refugee camps along the Thai-Burmese border.
The group's statement followed Friday attack by Burmese soldiers on ethnic Karenni refugee camps in Thailand.
Human Rights Watch said two were killed and nine others seriously injured in the attack which took place in the northern Thai border province of Mae Hong Son.

"Human Rights Watch is concerned by the attack by over 40 heavily-armed troops of (Burmese junta) on a Burmese refugee camp in Thailand...and calls on the Thai government to provide improved protection for this and other camps which are perilously close to Burma border," it said.
About 20,000 Karrenni refugees, fleeing earlier fighting with government forces in Burma, are living in a number of border camps in Thailand.
